title: Grade 4 CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — 6.1 Use of Social Media

pages.lesson:
PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

Social media and other digital tools can be used for good or for harm. In this sub-strand you will name digital devices used at home and at school, learn appropriate ways to use social media, and practise integrity by doing what is right even when nobody is watching the screen.

## Strand 6.0: Morality and Social Media
Sub-strand 6.1: Use of Social Media
Suggested lessons: 2

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) list digital devices used at home and school
b) discuss appropriate ways of using social media
c) apply the value of integrity when using social media
d) desire to do the right thing always even when no one is watching

## Key inquiry questions
1. Why should you use social media appropriately?

## Core competencies
• Communication: listening skills are enhanced as learners use social media devices to listen to a gospel song or watch a video clip based on the Bible.

## Values
• Responsibility: learners use social media responsibly.
• Integrity: learners use social media appropriately even when no one is watching them.

## Pertinent and contemporary issues
• Patriotism: learners show responsibility by using social media responsibly.

## Links to other learning areas
• Science and technology skills are applied as learners manipulate digital devices.
• English: communication skills are enhanced as learners engage in group discussions.

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 Christian Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 6.0 Morality and Social Media, Sub-strand 6.1 Use of Social Media

PAGE 2: Lesson 1: Digital devices and appropriate use

LESSON 1: DIGITAL DEVICES AND APPROPRIATE USE
=============================================

## What you will learn
• List digital devices used at home and at school.
• Describe appropriate ways of using social media.

Curriculum outcomes: a) list digital devices used at home and school; b) discuss appropriate ways of using social media

## Introduction
A phone, a tablet, a computer or a television can play a gospel song or a lesson. The same device can also carry a stranger's chat or a bad video. Appropriate use means choosing the good use and refusing the harmful one.

## Notes
### Digital devices
A digital device is a machine that stores or shares information using electronic signals. In groups, list devices you know or use. Not every home has all of them.

- Mobile phone or smartphone
- Tablet
- Computer or laptop
- Television
- Radio
- A camera, or the camera in a phone

At school you may use a computer, a tablet or a radio in a lesson. At home you may watch a television or use a parent's phone. Name only the devices you truly know. Do not pretend the school has a device it does not have.

### What social media is
Social media means ways of sending messages, photos and videos to other people through the internet, for example chats and video sites. Many Grade 4 learners meet it on an adult's phone.

### Appropriate ways to use it
Appropriate means fitting and right.

- Ask a parent, guardian or teacher before you use a device.
- Use it for learning, for a gospel song, or for a video clip based on the Bible.
- Keep the time short. Stop when the adult says stop.
- Be kind in any message you send. Do not insult or spread lies.
- Do not chat with strangers. A person online may not be who the photo shows, and some strangers want to harm children.
- Do not share your full name, the name of your school, your home area, your phone number or your photos with people you do not know.
- Do not open links sent by strangers.
- Do not look at or forward bad pictures.
- If a message frightens you or asks you to keep a secret, tell a parent or teacher at once.

Using a device to listen to a gospel song or to watch a Bible story is a good use. Chatting with a stranger is not. The device is not evil. The way we use it is the moral choice.

## Key words
• digital device — an electronic machine such as a phone, tablet, computer, radio or television
• social media — internet ways of sharing messages, photos and videos with other people
• appropriate — fitting and right for the user and for the situation
• stranger — a person you do not know, including a person who messages you online

## Worked examples

### Example 1
A message from someone you have never met says, "Send a photo of yourself and the name of your school." What is the appropriate response?

Working:
1. The sender is a stranger.
2. Sharing a photo and a school name with a stranger is not safe.
3. Appropriate use means refusing and telling an adult.

Answer: Do not send the photo or the school name. Tell a parent, guardian or teacher.

## Activity: Devices we know and how to use them well
You will need: Manila paper, A digital device if the teacher provides one, A gospel song or a Bible video clip
1. In groups, list some digital devices that you know or use at home and at school.
2. In pairs, discuss appropriate use of social media.
3. Say why you should not chat with strangers online.
4. With the teacher, use a digital device to listen to a gospel song or watch a video clip based on the Bible.

## Practice
1. Name four digital devices a learner might know at home or at school.
2. What is social media?
3. Give three appropriate ways of using social media or a digital device.
4. Why should you not chat with strangers online?

## Summary
• Digital devices include phones, tablets, computers, radios and televisions.
• Use them with permission, for learning and for what is good.
• Do not chat with strangers or give them your photos and private details.

### Answers to practice
1. Any four: mobile phone, tablet, computer, laptop, television, radio or camera.
2. Ways of sharing messages, photos and videos with other people through the internet.
3. Any three: ask permission, use it for learning or a gospel song or Bible video, keep the time short, be kind, and do not chat with strangers or share private details.
4. They may not be who they claim to be, and some strangers want to harm children.

PAGE 3: Lesson 2: Integrity when nobody is watching

LESSON 2: INTEGRITY WHEN NOBODY IS WATCHING
===========================================

## What you will learn
• Explain how integrity applies to social media.
• Choose to do right even when no adult is watching the screen.

Curriculum outcomes: c) apply the value of integrity when using social media; d) desire to do the right thing always even when no one is watching

## Introduction
It is easy to do right when a parent is looking over your shoulder. Integrity is doing the same right thing when the adult has walked into the kitchen and the screen is still on.

## Notes
### Integrity
Integrity means being honest and doing what is right even when it costs you, and even when no one sees. On social media, integrity looks like this:

- You do not open a bad video just because nobody is in the room.
- You do not send a cruel message and then pretend you did not.
- You do not use a parent's phone in secret after you were told to stop.
- You do not help a friend cheat by sending test answers.
- You tell the truth if you accidentally open something wrong.

God sees what people do not see. Integrity is living as if that is true, because it is true. The value is not fear of being caught only. It is a desire to do the right thing always.

### When no one is watching
Picture three moments:

1. The gospel song has ended. A new video, not chosen by your parent, starts to play and it is ungodly. Integrity switches it off.
2. A classmate messages, "Don't tell the teacher I took the pen." Integrity refuses to hide the wrong.
3. A stranger sends a friendly chat. Integrity does not reply and does not keep it a secret.

In each moment the device has not changed. The person using it has a choice. Appropriate use and integrity belong together. Appropriate use is the rule. Integrity is keeping the rule when it would be easy to break it.

### A simple promise
Before you touch a device, ask: Did an adult allow this? Is this kind? Would I be happy for my parent and for God to see it? If the answer is no, stop. Then tell a trusted adult about anything that already went wrong. Owning up is part of integrity too.

Using social media responsibly is a way of loving God and loving other people. It also keeps children safer. A learner who will not chat with strangers protects himself or herself and sets an example for friends.

## Key words
• integrity — doing what is right and honest even when nobody is watching
• responsible — using something in the way you were trusted to use it
• private details — facts such as your school, home, phone number and photos that strangers should not have

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Your parent leaves the room during a Bible video. The next clip is an ungodly movie, and no one will know if you watch it. What does integrity do?

Working:
1. Integrity means doing right even when no one is watching.
2. An ungodly movie is not an appropriate use of the device.
3. The right action does not depend on being caught.

Answer: Switch it off or go back to what you were allowed to watch, and tell your parent if you need help.

## Activity: Right use even when unseen
You will need: Exercise book, A digital device if the teacher provides one
1. In pairs, discuss appropriate use of social media, including what to do when an adult is not watching.
2. Say why you should not chat with strangers online.
3. Act the three moments: a bad video starts, a friend asks you to hide a wrong, a stranger sends a chat. Show the choice that has integrity.
4. If a device is available, listen again to a gospel song or a Bible clip, then stop when the teacher says stop.

## Practice
1. What is integrity?
2. Give two ways to show integrity when using social media.
3. A stranger's chat arrives while you are alone. What should you do, and why?
4. Why should you do the right thing even when no one is watching the screen?

## Summary
• Integrity is honesty and right action even when the screen is unwatched.
• Switch off what is ungodly, refuse secret chats, and do not hide other people's wrongs.
• Ask whether an adult allowed the use, whether it is kind, and whether God would be pleased.

### Answers to practice
1. Doing what is right and honest even when nobody is watching.
2. Any two: do not open bad videos in secret, do not send cruel messages, do not use a phone against an adult's instruction, do not hide a classmate's wrong, and do not reply to strangers.
3. Do not reply and do not keep it secret. Tell a parent or teacher. Strangers online may want to harm children, and integrity refuses hidden chats.
4. Because integrity means the right thing does not depend on being seen. God sees, and the choice still matters.
pages.quiz:
REVISION QUIZ — 6.1 USE OF SOCIAL MEDIA
========================================

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. Which of these is a digital device?
   A. A pullover
   B. A tablet
   C. An eraser
   D. A desk

2. Name two digital devices used at home or at school.

3. Social media is:
   A. A kind of school uniform
   B. Ways of sharing messages, photos and videos on the internet
   C. A church bench
   D. A Bible map

4. Which use of a device is appropriate?
   A. Chatting with a stranger
   B. Watching a Bible video with permission
   C. Sending a cruel message
   D. Sharing your home address online

5. Why should you not chat with strangers online?
   A. Because every stranger is a teacher
   B. Because they may not be who they seem, and some want to harm children
   C. Because phones cannot send messages
   D. Because the Bible forbids all songs

6. Which details should you not give to someone you do not know online?

7. Integrity when using social media means:
   A. Doing right only when a parent is watching
   B. Doing right even when nobody is watching
   C. Sending secret photos
   D. Copying a friend's test answers

8. An ungodly video starts while you are alone. What should you do?
   A. Watch it quickly
   B. Switch it off and tell a parent if you need help
   C. Call a stranger to discuss it
   D. Send it to the class

9. You want to do the right thing even when no one is watching. What value is that?
   A. Integrity
   B. Carelessness
   C. Secrecy
   D. Cheating

10. Before you use a device, which question helps you choose well?
pages.answers:
ANSWERS — 6.1 USE OF SOCIAL MEDIA
========================================

1. B. A tablet
   A tablet is an electronic device. The others are personal or school items.

2. Any two: phone, tablet, computer, laptop, television, radio or camera.
   Learners list devices they know or use.

3. B. Ways of sharing messages, photos and videos on the internet
   Social media shares messages and pictures through the internet.

4. B. Watching a Bible video with permission
   A Bible video with an adult's permission is a right use.

5. B. Because they may not be who they seem, and some want to harm children
   Strangers online are unsafe to chat with.

6. Your full name, school, home area, phone number and photos.
   Private details help a stranger to find or harm a child.

7. B. Doing right even when nobody is watching
   Integrity is right action without needing an audience.

8. B. Switch it off and tell a parent if you need help
   Integrity refuses the bad video even in private.

9. A. Integrity
   The desire to do right unseen is integrity.

10. Any one: Did an adult allow this? Is it kind? Would I want my parent and God to see it?
   These questions join appropriate use with integrity.
